originality.rationale: The strongest prior work, Gröchenig–Jaming (2016), classifies full sphere-measure Heisenberg uniqueness using Coxeter reflection groups: generic irrational-angle injectivity is known and not new. The novel candidate is the exact finite pure-cubic restriction that retains injectivity at all rational angles except 60 and 90 degrees, and its dimension-dependent nullity table. Han and Olofsson–Wittsten cover explicit sectoral harmonic nodal lines. This exact finite-degree table was not found in inspected work; historical implicit-equivalence risk remains.
residual_risks: Standard reflection-group or harmonic nodal-set literature may already contain an equivalent exact higher-dimensional two-equator criterion not retrieved in these searches.
Only the identified relevant portions of long primary sources were compared; absence of coverage from inspected sections does not eliminate implicit equivalent formulas elsewhere.

The Coxeter reflection framework from Gröchenig–Jaming (2016) may support an unstated low-degree representation-theoretic corollary exactly matching the table; a broader literature audit could reveal that implication.

value.rationale: Two complete great-sphere traces are a natural minimal observation geometry for pure-degree cubic harmonics. A complete necessary/sufficient rank classification discovers both dimension-dependent orthogonal nullity d-2 and fixed one-dimensional 60-degree nullity, and proves exact minimality for generic angles in all d>=3. This clarifies exact geometric reconstruction obstructions rather than merely computing an unmotivated numerical example. In the all-measures Heisenberg uniqueness problem, prior work already rules out rational-angle uniqueness; the cubic frequency cutoff restores recovery at every rational angle except two, a meaningful sharp filtered-versus-unrestricted distinction.
